newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Bank Austria to call CA shareholders meeting.
newsitem.headline: Bank Austria to call CA shareholders meeting.

text.p: Bank Austria, sketching its strategy after winning EU approval for its takeover of Creditanstalt, said on Monday it would call a meeting of Creditanstalt shareholders to select a new supervisory board.
Bank Austria chief executive Gerhard Randa told a news conference the bank would seek representation as quickly as possible on Creditanstalt's supervisory board.

"We are sending a letter to those responsible in Creditanstalt to call an extraordinary shareholders' meeting. There will be one point on the agenda -- the make-up of the supervisory board," Randa said.
"We want to be represented as quickly as possible -- so that we have access to information."
Bank Austria acquired the state's 70 percent of Creditanstalt ordinary voting shares in January. The European Commission gave the deal the green light last week.
Randa forecast the extraordinary meeting would take place on April 10 or 11.
He declined comment on changes to Creditanstalt's board.
Chief executive Guidon Schmidt-Chiari said over the weekend that he had tendered his resignation. The remaining board members have also offered to step down, according to Creditanstalt sources.
"The newly elected supervisory board will decide on the Creditanstalt board," Randa said. -- Janet McBride, Vienna newsroom +43-1 531 12 254
